description: Axiom rules bindings for Belgium's family-benefit content. Each binding names one rulespec-be module by repository-relative rulespec_path and SHA-256 at the pinned commit, the frame entity it sits on, the period label it runs for, and the variables a graph may request. The twelve modules are the ones whose programs the committed input surface compiles on the engine entity Child. No frame entity maps to Child, so each binding sits on the person entity and declares one binding-local view (views_note). Belgium has no composed transport graph yet: no node selects a binding, and nothing here runs until the graph change adds the selector producers, the closure node and the rules nodes. axiom_input_closure.json closes every Child root of these modules.

rulespec.verification: The commit is on origin/main of rulespec-be (git branch -r --contains), and is main's head. The committed input surface was generated at the pin, and each of the twelve bound modules' SHA-256 at the pin equals the surface's.

engine.status: Pinned at New Zealand's engine pin (nz/axiom_rules_bindings.json). commit is the axiom-rules-engine commit that Belgium's input surface and input closure record. wheel_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the dense-extension wheel the NZ hub built at that commit (CPython 3.14, macOS arm64), the wheel whose extension generated Belgium's input surface. axiom_engine_ref records both as declared and hashes no installed wheel. build_transport_registry also needs the unit entity that entity_names_note describes, so no registry builds from this file before it lands.

entity_names_note: entity_names holds the two frame entities the axiom:be mapping maps. build_transport_registry requires it to name exactly the transport schema's entities: person, household and each unit entity the benefit unit rule declares (transport/registry.py, build_transport_registry; frame/unit_construction.py, MultiUnitRule.entity_schema). Belgium has no benefit_unit_rule.json yet. The change that adds it also adds its entity here, under an engine name other than Child, since the registry refuses a view whose logical entity a frame entity maps to.
period_note: Every variable these bindings request runs by Month, so the one period label names a month: January 2026, with explicit bounds, because the registry takes no period without them. The kind is calendar_month, the name rulespec-be's own tests give the custom monthly period they run these modules over (for example be-bru/statutes/family_benefits/eligibility.test.yaml). At the surface's engine commit 753ce7d9ac4cfb161f6aa4f281f5a3980e67a57d, the Python extension reads any kind other than month, benefit_week and tax_year as a custom period of that name (python-ext/src/lib.rs:985-992). No rule version in the twelve modules starts after 2026-01-01, so each month of 2026 reads the same versions. A graph that needs an annual amount multiplies the monthly output by twelve in a declared transform. No binding requests the modules' Year rules (such as the annual age supplements, the German-speaking annual supplement and the Flemish participation supplement) or any birth or adoption premium.

input_surface.notes: The committed input surface was generated at rulespec-be 632e1da1110ba881c68165e0cd3c2287b5b8ab08, the pin. root_input_count is the size of each module's canonical input surface, all of it on Child.

views_note: Each view's selector is a bool person column that no node produces yet. The selectors block gives each column's meaning; the graph change that follows adds the producers and sets each cut-off. None of the regional modules bound here reads a birth date, and every amount they return is their reform scheme's. Flanders and Wallonia keep an older cohort on the old LGAF-based amounts (Flemish decree article 210, Walloon decree article 120), so those two selectors leave that cohort out, as their meanings say. Brussels and the German-speaking Community adjust amounts instead, which no selector cut-off can express: Brussels ordinance article 35 takes 10 euros off each article 7 base amount for a child born before 1 December 2019, Brussels article 39 keeps the LGAF payment rules where the December 2019 LGAF rate gives more than articles 7 to 13, and German-speaking decree article 111 computes a transition amount from the LGAF benefits one person received for December 2018. rulespec-be encodes the Brussels article 35 deduction and a one-child slice of the Flemish and Walloon old-cohort amounts (first-rank 2025 amounts, chosen by age rather than birth date) in be/statutes/family_benefits/child_benefit_base_2025.yaml, which these bindings don't cover, and encodes neither article 39 nor article 111. A view's root inputs read the person columns of the same names (docs/transport-declared-units.md, Binding-local views), so the closure gives a name one default in every module that reads it. Each outside value is the output's value for a person outside the view: 0.0 for a Money output and 0 for a Count output. At the surface's engine commit 753ce7d9ac4cfb161f6aa4f281f5a3980e67a57d, formula lowering reads a rule's dtype through a match that has no Count arm and falls through to Decimal (src/formula.rs:1419-1430). An integer 0 casts without loss to a decimal output and to an integer one, so it holds whichever dtype a later engine pin gives a Count.

selectors.brussels_family_benefits_child_candidate: True for a person the Brussels scheme's modules run on as Child: a person domiciled in the Brussels-Capital Region whom the scheme's age and status rules could reach. The modules decide entitlement. The selector keeps other regions' residents out, and the closure's domicile default relies on that.
selectors.german_speaking_community_family_benefit: True for a person the German-speaking Community scheme's modules run on as Child: a person domiciled in the German language region whom the scheme's age and status rules could reach. The modules decide entitlement. The selector keeps other regions' residents out, and the closure's domicile default relies on that.
selectors.flanders_family_benefits_child_candidate: True for a person the Flemish scheme's modules run on as Child: a person domiciled in the Dutch language region whom the scheme's age and status rules could reach, other than a child that decree article 210 §1 keeps on the old child benefit. The modules decide entitlement. The selector keeps other regions' residents out, and the closure's domicile default relies on that. Article 210 §1 covers a child born before 1 January 2019 who met the old rules' conditions on 31 December 2018: article 8's conditions still decide that child's entitlement, but article 210 §2 sets the amount from the old rules, and article 13 withholds from that child the base amount that both monthly amounts these bindings request include. Every Flemish child aged 8 or over in 2026 was born before 2019.
selectors.wallonia_family_benefits_child_candidate: True for a person the Walloon scheme's modules run on as Child: a person domiciled in the French language region whom the scheme's age and status rules could reach and who was born on or after 1 January 2020, the reform date from which these modules' rules apply. The modules decide entitlement. The selector keeps other regions' residents out, and the closure's domicile default relies on that. Decree article 120 keeps LGAF articles 40 to 50septies, 52 to 55 and 56ter to 76bis applying to a child born before that date, so that child's base amount and age supplements come from the LGAF, not from the decree's base amount that both monthly amounts these bindings request include; article 121 lets the decree's article 5 prevail for a child who reaches 18 in the reform year. Every Walloon child aged 7 or over in 2026 was born before 2020.
selectors.belgium_lgaf_child_candidate: True for a person the federal LGAF amount schedule runs on as Child. No bound module imports this schedule, and the routing bridge returns none of its outputs. Its one importer at the pin, be/statutes/family_benefits/guaranteed_family_benefits.yaml, describes a pre-2019 guarantee layer, and the committed surface marks that module dense_unsupported. The monthly total this binding requests holds no entitlement test, so a 2026 graph selects no one: its producer writes false for every person, or no node requests the binding.
selectors.belgium_family_benefits_child_candidate: True for a person the regional routing bridge runs on as Child. The bridge picks a scheme from belgium_family_benefits_region, which the closure defaults to 99, a code outside 0 to 3, so the bridge pays 0 to every child it runs on until a graph node supplies each child's code. Until then the four regional eligibility bindings give the national amount under their own selectors, and a request for this binding adds nothing to them. Once a node supplies the codes, this selector must also leave out the Flemish and Walloon older cohort, as those schemes' selectors do, or the bridge would pay that cohort the reform base amount.

bindings.notes: The article 7 base amount, with no entitlement gate. Request it only to split the eligible amount into base and supplement; never sum it as spending. brussels_family_benefits_eligibility reaches it through its imports.

The scheme's payable monthly amount (the article 4, 25 and 26 gate on the article 7 base plus the article 9 supplement) and the 0/1 entitlement it rests on. Both rules hold one version, from 2025-09-01.
The ungated sum of the article 7 base and the article 9 supplement. A graph that wants spending requests brussels_family_benefits_eligibility's eligible amount, which imports this output.
The article 9 social supplement, with no entitlement gate. Under the closure's income default it is 0 for every child, until a graph node supplies household income.

The monthly total before the eligibility module's entitlement gate (the base amount plus the monthly supplements, each behind conditions of its own). A graph that wants spending requests german_speaking_community_family_benefits_eligibility's eligible amount, which imports this output. The module's Year rules and its birth and adoption premiums are not requested.
The scheme's payable monthly amount behind the articles 6 and 9 to 14 gate, and the 0/1 statutory base entitlement it rests on.

The ungated monthly total (the base amount plus the orphan, disability, foster-care and social supplements). A graph that wants spending requests flanders_family_benefits_eligibility's eligible amount, which imports this output. The annual participation supplement, a Year rule with no entitlement gate, is not requested.
The scheme's payable monthly amount behind the article 8 gate, and the 0/1 entitlement it rests on.

The ungated monthly total (the base amount plus the monthly supplements). A graph that wants spending requests wallonia_family_benefits_eligibility's eligible amount, which imports this output. The article 17 annual age supplement, a Year rule with no entitlement gate, is not requested, so Walloon amounts leave it out.
The scheme's payable monthly amount behind the articles 4 to 6 gate, and the 0/1 entitlement it rests on.

The federal amount schedule of the Loi generale relative aux allocations familiales. The one variable requested, the monthly total, holds no entitlement rule or event test, and age only picks its article 44 age supplement (0 below 6), so at the closure's rank default of 1 it pays every row the view admits; the article 44ter annual supplement, which no binding requests, has age and beneficiary conditions of its own. No bound module imports it and the routing bridge returns none of its outputs, so no 2026 node should request it; added to a regional amount it would count a child twice. The binding and its closure entries exist so that the module's 18 Child roots are closed. The birth allowance and adoption premium read no birth or adoption event and are never requested.

The bridge over the four regional schemes: it returns the chosen scheme's eligible monthly amount by belgium_family_benefits_region (0 Flanders, 1 Brussels, 2 Wallonia, 3 German-speaking Community; any other code returns 0). Its ungated output skips the schemes' entitlement gates and is not requested. No graph may add the bridge's output to the four regional amounts.

keying_note: Each Axiom-bound node is to carry its own binding entry, the rulespec and engine pin blocks, the entity names and its period, plus a digest of exactly those values, never this file's SHA-256. Otherwise an edit to one scheme's binding would re-key every other scheme's nodes. Which graph nodes consume which binding is the composer's business, not this resource's.
